name: Handing Off to Kindergarten
title: Handing Off to Kindergarten
answer: Handing off to kindergarten means using AI to help preschool teachers write short, careful profiles of each child so kindergarten teachers begin the year already knowing their strengths, interests, goals, and what helps them feel settled. It matters because the preschool-to-kindergarten move is one of the biggest transitions in a child's life, and good information can make it smoother. Screening results can also shape playful, brief practice in the first weeks, with the goal of a confident start rather than an early test.

sections.body: The transition from preschool to kindergarten is one of the largest changes a child experiences, and the quality of information passed between teachers can ease it. AI can assist a preschool teacher in drafting a brief profile of each child that covers strengths, interests, current goals, and the things that help the child feel settled. The kindergarten teacher then begins the year with some knowledge of each child instead of starting cold. This solves the problem of children arriving as strangers to their new teacher and of useful preschool knowledge being lost over the summer. The profile is meant to be written with care, describing what a child can do and what helps rather than applying labels that could follow the child unfairly.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: A preschool teacher drafts a short profile for each child and passes it to the kindergarten teacher, who starts the year already knowing something about every child. Names appear during drafting and are put back in only in the final version, which is stored in the district's own system. Families see the profile and can add to it. Screening results can also shape the first weeks: if a spring screener shows a child needs more practice with letter sounds, the teacher can use an approved tool to create short practice activities for the summer or the first month. That practice should be playful and brief, and a teacher should review it, with the aim of a confident start rather than an early test.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no study, figure, or finding for this idea, and it carries no evidence label. It rests on practice rather than research, describing what teachers can do to smooth the preschool-to-kindergarten transition and how screening results might inform the first weeks.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The profile must be written with care. Names come out during drafting and go back in only in the final version stored in the district's own system. The profile should describe what the child can do and what helps, not labels that could follow a child unfairly. Families should see the profile and have a chance to add to it. Any practice activities drawn from screening results should be playful and brief, and a teacher should review them, keeping the goal on a confident start rather than an early test.
